name: Reactivity

hero.title: Delete useMemo, useCallback and every dependency array.
hero.lede: Signals know who reads them, so derived values and effects keep themselves up to date and a write touches only what depends on it. It is the engine under every Pyreon app, with no dependencies, and it runs on its own in Node, Bun, a worker or a script.

why.title: Less to write, less to get wrong.

items.title: Nothing to list
items.text: A computed or effect subscribes to exactly the signals it read on its last run. When a branch stops reading a signal, the dependency is dropped, so there is no array to keep in sync and no stale closure to chase.

items.title: One write, one update
items.text: `batch()` groups writes and runs each effect once with the final values. A diamond (`a` feeding two computeds that feed one effect) never shows a half-updated state.

items.title: Cheap where lists are big
items.text: A signal with one subscriber keeps it in an inline slot and allocates no `Set`. `createSelector` re-runs 2 rows when a selection moves, not 10,000.

items.title: Ask why it ran
items.text: Call `why()` before a write and the console names each signal that changed: `[pyreon:why] "first": "Ada" → "Grace" (1 subscriber)`. `inspectSignal` and `getReactiveTrace` go deeper.

difference.title: The same cart, with and without dependency arrays.

api.title: Grouped the way you use them.

limits.title: Mutating in place needs trigger()
limits.text: Signals compare with `Object.is`, so `set(sameObject)` does nothing. Update immutably, or mutate and call `trigger()`.

limits.title: Read inside a tracking scope
limits.text: A signal read in a plain function body subscribes nothing. Read it in an effect, a computed or JSX.

limits.title: A new object every time means a notify every time
limits.text: A computed that returns a fresh object or array notifies on each recompute. Pass `equals` when readers should skip identical results.

limits.title: Cheap to update, not the cheapest to create
limits.text: Creating a signal costs about 5× what Preact Signals does (63 vs 13 ns on V8). Create them once, not inside hot loops.

end.title: Your components stop re-rendering. You stop wondering why they did.

benchmarks.rival: vs Preact Signals and Solid · V8 (Node 26), Pyreon bundled · plus the 10-framework row board
benchmarks.h: Fastest where an update spends its time: propagation.
benchmarks.p: Pyreon wins the work a real update runs through: effect propagation, batching and the computed diamond. It loses raw signal creation (4.8×), deep unobserved chains (1.42×) and wide fan-out (3–4%), and those rows stay in the table.

comingFrom.title: State you can read right after you write it
comingFrom.note: `count()` reads, `count.set(v)` writes, `count.update(fn)` derives. Calling `count(5)` only reads, so writes are always `.set`.

comingFrom.title: Derived values without a dependency list
comingFrom.before: const total = useMemo(() => price * qty, [price, qty])
comingFrom.note: A computed is lazy and cached: it recomputes only when read after a dependency changed. If it returns a new object each time, pass `{ equals }` so readers skip identical results.

comingFrom.title: Side effects that re-run on their own
comingFrom.note: The effect re-runs when `delay` changes, cleaning up first. Effects run synchronously after a write (or once at the end of a `batch`), and one created inside a component is disposed with it.

recipes.title: Selection in a 10,000-row list
recipes.text: A plain `selected() === id` check in every row re-runs all 10,000 rows on each click. `createSelector` keeps a bucket per value and notifies only the row that lost the selection and the one that gained it.

recipes.title: Search that never shows a stale answer
recipes.text: `createResource` refetches when its source changes and ignores any response that arrives after a newer request started, so a slow reply to "p" can't overwrite the answer to "py".

recipes.title: A choice that resets when its options change
recipes.text: `linked()` follows a source like a computed but can be overwritten like a signal. Keep the user's pick while it is still offered; fall back to the first option when it is not.
recipes.code:
import { signal, linked } from '@pyreon/reactivity'

const sizes = signal(['S', 'M', 'L'])
const size = linked(sizes, (opts, prev): string =>
  prev && opts.includes(prev.value) ? prev.value : (opts[0] ?? ''),
)

size.set('L')
console.log(size()) // 'L'
sizes.set(['M', 'L', 'XL'])
console.log(size()) // 'L' (still offered, kept)
sizes.set(['XS', 'S'])
console.log(size()) // 'XS' (gone, reset)

faq.q: Can I use it without the rest of Pyreon?
faq.a: Yes. It has no dependencies and no DOM code: `bun add @pyreon/reactivity` and use it in Node, Bun, a worker or a CLI. Pyreon's components, router, forms, queries and stores all build on it.
Yes. A write runs the effects that depend on it before `set()` returns, unless you are inside `batch()`, which runs them once at the end. `await nextTick()` waits for the DOM after a write.

faq.q: How does it compare with Preact Signals and Solid?
faq.a: Same model, measured: about 2.1× Preact on effect propagation, 1.95× on batching and 1.3× on a computed diamond (V8, two runs). It loses signal creation (4.8×), deep unobserved chains (1.42×) and wide fan-out by 1.03×. Solid is behind on every row except creation.
A signal is a function, so reading it is a call and passing it around passes the live value. There are no proxies unless you ask for one with `createStore`.

faq.q: Does it work in the iOS and Android builds?
faq.a: Yes, on the experimental native targets: `signal` and `computed` compile to SwiftUI and Compose state through PMTC, `effect` re-runs when what it read changes, and `batch` lowers too. `linked()`, coming in the next release, has no native lowering yet, and the compiler warns by name when it meets one.
